title: The 4-Text Sequence That Revives Dead Estimates

slides.headline: The 4-text sequence that revives dead estimates
slides.body: Steal this. Word for word. (Texts get 45–55% response rates. Calls get 20–30%.)

slides.headline: TEXT 1 — Day 1 (same day as the quote)
slides.body: "Hi [Name], it's [You] from [Shop]. Great meeting you today — your quote for the [system] is attached. Any questions at all, just text me back here. No rush."

slides.headline: TEXT 2 — Day 3
slides.body: "Hi [Name], quick check-in — did any questions come up about the quote? Happy to walk through financing options too. Most folks are surprised what the monthly comes to."

slides.headline: TEXT 3 — Day 7
slides.body: "Hi [Name], [You] from [Shop]. Totally understand this is a big decision. One thing worth knowing: install slots for the next 2 weeks are filling up. Want me to pencil you in while you decide?"

slides.headline: TEXT 4 — Day 14
slides.body: "Hi [Name], last note from me so I'm not a pest. If now's not the time, no problem at all — I'll check back before summer. If anything changed, I'm one text away."
slides.footer: THE GRACEFUL EXIT (gets replies more than any other text)

slides.headline: Why this works
slides.body: 80% of deals take 8–12 touches; most shops make 1. SMS gets 45–55% responses vs 20–30% for calls. Automated sequences convert ~2.8× better than one-off attempts. A 10-point close-rate lift is worth ~$28K/mo for a mid-size shop.

slides.headline: Set it up once. It runs on every quote. Forever.
slides.body: Any modern field-service tool or automation platform can send these automatically on day 1/3/7/14. Save this post — it IS the template. And comment "AUDIT" if you want to know what else in your shop should run on autopilot.
